title: Semantics in enabling/disabling port message queues and the has_been_shipped flag in MessagePorts
body:
The [port message queue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/comms.html#port-message-queue) has an enabled/disabled state, and is initially disabled. From my IRC conversations with @annevk, when a task is queued on the port message queue while it's disabled, the queue should buffer it, until the port is enabled, then the queued task would be processed sequentially as they were queued.

Thus far, it's clear, but the associated MessagePort of the port message queue has a [has_been_shipped](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/comms.html#has-been-shipped) flag as well, which, from what my spec reading tells me, does something similar, in that a MessagePort that has not been shipped will buffer the incoming tasks on an [unshipped port message queue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/comms.html#unshipped-port-message-queue), and when it is finally shipped, the tasks in the unshipped port message queue will be re-queued on the port message queue. Am I correct in this interpretation? Are the tasks dropped instead once they are queued on the unshipped port message queue?

Here are the relevant test cases in the web platform tests repository: https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/webmessaging/message-channels. In particular, 002.html tests what happens when one tries to post a message on a port that has not been enabled. 004.html tests what happens in a cross-origin context, but is not sufficient because it does not tests for the behaviour of the `has_been_shipped` flag.
